name: TaoPad (TPAD) tax-ETH extraction: Yoink replays the operator's failed tx
race_type_reason: The counterparty is the TaoPad operator (not a hacker). Its tx failed on chain (out of gas, block 19226482); Yoink replayed the same victim-protocol call sequence 21 blocks / 252 s later with a higher gas limit. Nothing was pending in between and no other tx called the vulnerable function.
one_liner: TaoPad's own operator tx to pull the token's 29.2 ETH tax balance ran out of gas; Yoink replayed its calls 4 min later (net 26.32 ETH) and returned it all the next day after the team wrote to it.

attacker.none_reason: No hostile attacker in this event. The racing counterparty is the project's operator (below). The earlier third-party exploit of the TPAD token that TaoPad mentions is outside the scope and not identified here.

counterparty.kind: project operator (the protocol extracting its own accumulated tax ETH)
counterparty.label: taopad.eth (TaoPad team)

txs.role: operator funds helper deployer 0x397c9e1c with 0.12 ETH
operator: helper.execute() with 1 ETH, public mempool, out of gas in the second swap
operator: TPAD.setPoolFee(0) after Yoink's tx (message: 'so nobody could exploit Tpad again')

mempool_note: mempool-dumpster covers 2024-02-14 (csv + sourcelog). The operator's failed tx was seen publicly by 6 sources (first 13:23:12.276Z, local), 10.7 s before inclusion. Yoink's tx 0x5853b7a0 is not in the archive (private flow), so its own first-seen / bid time is unknown.

trigger.note: kind is null on purpose: the first-seen above is the OPERATOR's public tx, but Yoink did not pre-empt it as a pending tx. It was mined and failed (block 19226482, 13:23:23Z) 252 s before Yoink's block 19226503 (13:27:35Z; 262.7 s after first seen), with no operator tx pending in between. Recorded to document the gap, not as a trigger.

attacker_block_note: The racing tx is the operator's reverted execute() at block 19226482 index 0; Yoink landed 21 blocks AFTER it (blocks_ahead = -21).

auction.auction_note: 138 bids / 21 builders on Flashbots' archive. The winning block (blockbeelder via Ultrasound, 1.4032 ETH to the proposer, contains Yoink's tx) was submitted once at +380 ms; best other bid 0.0222 ETH (beaverbuild, +320 ms): the block was ~63x the next best bid. The bot's own submission time and whether other builders also held its bundle are unknown (relays do not publish bid contents). Not a competition for a pending attacker tx.

loot.gross_loot_method: WETH.withdraw ETH delivered to Yoink's contract in the tx trace (29.5056 ETH: 29.1789 from the TPAD token's accumulated ETH balance sold through the in-tx Uniswap V3 pool + 0.3267 recovered liquidity) minus the 1.0 ETH working capital it sent into the router/position manager. This is also the 'profit' of Yoink's per-mille bribe rule: 49/1000 x 28.5056 = 1.3968 = the coinbase transfer.

captured_native.desc: ETH balance of the TPAD token contract (accumulated trading taxes), swapped via a pool created inside the tx and withdrawn as WETH

loot.loot_note: bot_net = gross 28.5056 - coinbase 1.3968 - gas 0.7847 (29.38M gas at base fee 26.71 gwei, priority fee 0) = 26.3242 ETH. No builder refund in this block (13 txs; the only builder-sent tx is the proposer payment).

fate.returned_to: taopad.eth 0x98915686e23032a1d3b8596badd7fadf147d5c00 (the operator wallet that sent the failed tx)
fate.returned_desc: Yoink sent exactly 26.32 ETH to taopad.eth on 2024-02-15T12:53:35Z (block 19233454, tx 0xa0346352...) with the message 'Thanks for the explanation, sent back the entire bot profit.' 99.98% of the bot's net 26.3242 ETH, 92.3% of the 28.5056 ETH gross after working capital (the bribe and gas are sunk). Sequence: TaoPad messaged Yoink at 2024-02-14T13:54:59Z (27 min after the tx); Yoink asked for details 'to make sure it wasn't a failed rug attempt' (20:50:47Z); TaoPad explained at 2024-02-15 09:26-09:37Z; Yoink returned at 12:53:35Z.
fate.bounty_desc: No bounty; Yoink kept only the ~0.0042 ETH difference between the 26.32 round number and its 26.3242 net.

returned_txs.note: Yoink -> taopad.eth, 'sent back the entire bot profit'

fate.public_statement: On-chain messages only (research/lineages/yoink_messages.json; decoded from the Yoink EOA txlist). TaoPad: 'we have been frontran by your bot' / 'we have to extract the rewards ourselves taking advantage of this vulnerability'; Yoink: 'Thanks for the explanation, sent back the entire bot profit.'
fate.return_status_rule: returned = everything went back to the victim side except a bounty the victim agreed to or offered; partial = some came back, otherwise; none = known zero within the documented search window; unknown = unresolved

rawref_gaps.why: Yoink's tx is not in mempool-dumpster; what triggered it (operator's public tx, helper deployment, setPoolFee or independent discovery) is unknown
no USD price source saved; 29.18 ETH is the TPAD tax balance taken
TaoPad says the token was exploited weeks earlier; not identified or verified here; no web source fetched (search budget exhausted)

discrepancies: yoink_more_incidents.json calls this 'not an exploit by Yoink: it front-ran the project extracting its own rewards'. The chain shows a replay AFTER the project's tx had already failed (21 blocks, 252 s later), not a front-run of a pending tx.

TaoPad's message says its tx failed because it 'was frontran'. Its tx reverted out of gas on its own (gas limit 29,792,302; the failing frame is the second swap, which needed more than the ~10.06M gas it was given); Yoink's equivalent swap used 10,041,501 with a 30,000,000 limit.
leads file est_profit 28.506 ETH is the gross-profit estimate (coinbase / 0.049); the bot's net after bribe and gas is 26.3242 ETH.
evidence_notes: incidents/taopad-2024/call_diff.json: 9 victim-protocol calls of Yoink's tx pair one-to-one with calls of the operator's tx (same target, selector; 4 byte-identical after normalising the two contracts; the others differ in swap/mint deadline = each tx's block timestamp, one amount-bound word, approve amount). The ETH amounts 0.6667 + 0.3333 and distribute(0) are identical. The operator's trace stops at the second swap (out of gas); Yoink's continues with decreaseLiquidity/collect and two WETH.withdraw.

site/raw/rpc/taopad_tf_token_19226300_19226700.json: the only calls to TPAD.distribute (0x91c05b0b) in blocks 19226300-19226700 are the operator's reverted one (19226482) and Yoink's (19226503): no other racer, no earlier exploiter in the window.

site/raw/etherscan/taopad_victim_txlist_19200000_19240000.json: operator nonces 451 (fund deployer, 19226381), 453 (execute, failed), 452 setPoolFee(100) at 19226402 before, 454 setPoolFee(0) at 19226577 after Yoink: no pending operator tx between the failure and Yoink.

TPAD token source (verified on Etherscan): distribute(uint256 amountOutMinimum) is public, swaps the contract's whole ETH balance to the reward token through Uniswap V3 at the operator-set poolFee with the caller's minimum-out. TaoPad set poolFee to 0 after the incident ('so nobody could exploit Tpad contract again').
